chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Kufi al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abu Abdillah, from al-Qasim al-Hadrami, from Salih ibn Sahl, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'And We conveyed to the Children of Israel in the Book that you will surely cause corruption in the land twice,' he said: The killing of Ali and the stabbing of al-Hasan. And 'And you will surely be arrogant with great arrogance,' he said: The killing of al-Husayn (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: What are the two corruptions in the land mentioned in Surah Al-Isra verse 4 according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh presents this interpretation of Quran 17:4 as a key verse regarding the Ahl al-Bayt, linking the 'two corruptions' to the martyrdom of Imam Ali and the stabbing of Imam Hasan, while 'great arrogance' refers to the martyrdom of Imam Husayn. This exegesis highlights the centrality of the Imams' sacrifices in Shia theological understanding of Quranic history. The narrative underscores the continuity of divine trial and martyrdom within the Prophet's household.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Kūfi Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Mūsā ibn Sa’dān, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Qāsim Al-Ḥaďrami, from Sāliḥ ibn Sahl, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: “We announced to the children of Israel in the book: ‘You will certainly make mischief in the land twice” [17:4].

The first “mischief” refers to killing ‘Ali (the Commander of the Believers (a.s.)) and the second “mischief” refers to stabbing Ḥasan (a.s.). “And you will certainly become exceedingly arrogant” [17:4] refers to killing Ḥusain (a.s.).
